material: cervical epithelium / HSIL / SCC, rRNA-depleted total RNA
reason: Four groups, 6 cases each, one protocol: HPV-NEGATIVE normal epithelium, HPV16-POSITIVE normal epithelium, HPV16+ HSIL, HPV16+ squamous carcinoma. The HPV16-positive NORMAL arm is the direct cervical counterpart to skin carriage -- virus present, no disease -- and the series carries the presence-to-activity gradient inside a single controlled design. rRNA-depletion (not polyA) also favours viral read recovery.

material: hysterectomy tissue, ectocervix n=10 + endocervix n=15
reason: Genuine normal cervical tissue from women not on hormonal contraception/treatment, sampled at hysterectomy for benign gynaecological indications. Not cancer, not a line. Anatomically split ecto/endo, which the skin comparison does not need but does not hurt.

HR-HPV-positive patients followed 6-12 months with clearance-vs-persistence outcome. Carriage rather than carcinoma, and SURFACE-sampled material -- the closest public analogue to Shen's skin-surface sampling, so the presence-vs-activity contrast is drawn on comparable material rather than across sampling modes.

Cervical mucosal gene expression in women with/without S. haematobium. The automated triage called this "tumour" on keyword bleed; it is NOT cancer. Largest non-malignant cervical mucosa set found, with an internal infected/uninfected split.
